page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.3xlarge is a compute-oriented virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores and 12 threads powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base clock of 2.9 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 48 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction extensions, including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 24.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (2.0 GB per core). There is no integrated local storage, requiring network block storage for persistence, while network interfaces provide a 4 Gbps baseline throughput without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.c7se.3xlarge firmly within median performance brackets for its hardware classification. In CPU testing, the system recorded 1870.18 on single-core and 11653.27 on multi-core stress-ng suites, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 7822.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 16449.23. Memory bandwidth delivers 82.59 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 52.05 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific benchmarks indicate capable throughput, achieving 16.85 GB/sec in static web serving and 11.96 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Compression throughput reaches 27.97 GB/sec for single-threaded gzip and 63.89 GB/sec for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Small LLM inference demonstrates usable throughput for 135M parameter models, but execution slows considerably on 7B models (24.22 tokens/sec for prompt ingestion), reflecting the absence of discrete GPU acceleration.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated core architecture and compute-leaning memory profile reduce overhead for CPU-heavy tasks without paying for surplus RAM. However, the lack of local NVMe storage introduces I/O dependencies on remote network volumes, and the 24.0 GB memory capacity limits its suitability for memory-dense datasets. The ecs.c7se.3xlarge is functionally suited for horizontally scaled web servers, application backend microservices, software compilation and CI/CD pipelines, cryptographic offloading, and distributed batch processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.3xlarge is a compute-focused virtual instance equipped with 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores, powered by a 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor. Operating on x86_64 architecture with 48 MB of L3 cache, the system incorporates AVX-512 and VNNI vector instruction sets. Memory capacity is configured at 24.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio characteristic of compute-optimized hardware. Network connectivity delivers a 4 Gbps baseline throughput, and the instance operates entirely without integrated local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage needs. Benchmark testing reflects consistent mid-tier performance across single-core and multi-core computational evaluations, static web serving throughput reaching 16.85 GB/sec, and steady Redis operations. While smaller language models execute smoothly, larger model inference is constrained by core count and lack of hardware acceleration. The instance is structured for web servers, continuous integration pipelines, batch processing, and compute-bound microservices requiring dedicated execution cores.
